method: Page fetched directly with curl and converted from HTML to text. Every claim is verbatim-checked against that file with scripts/verify.py. Prose paraphrases; source_text stays verbatim. THREE DOSE TABLES (maintenance appendix, macrogol sachet disimpaction schedule, OsmoLax scoop schedule) are tables rendered as text: the values are verbatim and the schedules are quoted as contiguous blocks, but COLUMN ALIGNMENT IS A TRANSCRIPTION RISK and a person must confirm the grid against the source page before prescribing. The source was last updated March 2020, six years before retrieval.

claims.claim: Constipation affects a third of children and clusters around solids, toilet training and school
claims.source_text: Constipation affects 1/3 of children and frequently occurs during the introduction of solid foods, toilet training and school

claims.claim: Symptoms are under reported
claims.source_text: Symptoms of constipation are under reported

claims.claim: Increasing dietary fibre is not adequate treatment
claims.source_text: Increasing dietary fibre is not an adequate treatment for constipation

claims.claim: No need to increase fluid beyond maintenance
claims.source_text: There is no need to increase fluid intake beyond daily maintenance fluid requirements

claims.claim: Suppositories and enemas should be avoided
claims.source_text: Rectal treatment with suppositories or enemas should be avoided

claims.claim: Long term laxatives are safe and do not cause a lazy bowel
claims.source_text: Osmotic and lubricant laxatives are usually required on a long term basis (months to years). Reassure parents that this is safe and doesn't produce a 'lazy bowel'

claims.claim: Stopping laxatives too early causes recurrence
claims.source_text: A common cause of recurrence is stopping laxatives too early … Treatment is usually required for several months and if stopped early, may lead to recurrence

claims.claim: Titrate to one soft easy bowel action per day
claims.source_text: Medications are often required and should be titrated to achieve one, soft, easy to pass bowel action per day

claims.claim: Diagnosis is clinical; no internal examination or X-ray required
claims.source_text: The diagnosis is made clinically. Internal examination and X-ray are not required

claims.claim: Internal examination needs senior consultation first
claims.source_text: Internal examination should not be performed without first consulting a senior clinician

claims.claim: Investigations not routinely required
claims.source_text: Investigations are not routinely required

claims.claim: Rome IV criteria
claims.source_text: Must include ≥2 criteria for at least 1 month in infants or 2 months in older children … 2 stools/week … History of retentive posturing or excessive volitional stool retention (ie withholding or incomplete evacuation) … History of painful or hard bowel movements … History of large-diameter stools … Presence of a large faecal mass in the rectum

claims.claim: Additional criterion in toilet-trained children
claims.source_text: At least 1 episode per week of soiling/incontinence after the acquisition of toileting skills

claims.claim: Infant dyschezia is not constipation
claims.source_text: Healthy infants (<6 months) can strain and cry before passing soft stools (dyschezia). Unless the stools are also hard, this is not constipation and will self-resolve

claims.claim: Normal stool frequency including breastfed infants
claims.source_text: Most children defaecate at least every 2-3 days however breastfed babies may defaecate as infrequently as once per week

claims.claim: The withholding cycle
claims.source_text: Young children may ignore the urge to defaecate, causing a build-up of large hard bowel actions. When this leads to painful defaecation it may cause apprehension, stool retention and passage of further hard stool

claims.claim: Red flags
claims.source_text: Infants presenting <6 weeks of age - should be discussed with a senior doctor … Delayed passage of meconium - most infants pass meconium in the first 24 hours of life (consider Hirschsprung disease or anorectal malformation) … Ribbon like stools - consider anorectal malformation … Abdominal mass (not consistent with large faecal mass)

claims.claim: Organic causes medical and surgical
claims.source_text: Coeliac disease … Hypothyroidism … Hypercalcaemia … Slow-transit constipation … Hirschsprung disease … Meconium ileus … Anatomic malformations of anus … Spinal cord abnormalities

claims.claim: Examination includes spine and neurology
claims.source_text: Lower back/spine - consider occult spinal dysraphism/tethered cord … Neurology - assessment of lower limbs, observation of gait

claims.claim: ASD and ADHD increase risk of functional constipation
claims.source_text: children with autism spectrum disorders and attention deficit / hyperactive disorder have an increased risk of functional constipation

claims.claim: Toileting position advice
claims.source_text: Position - footstool to ensure knees are higher than hips. Lean forward and put elbows on knees

claims.claim: Toilet sits regimen
claims.source_text: Toilet sits - up to 5 minutes, three times a day, preferably after meals … Encourage child to bulge out their abdomen. Praise child for sitting on toilet. Ensure toileting remains a positive experience

claims.claim: Delay toilet training until painless soft stools
claims.source_text: Delay toilet training attempts until child is painlessly passing soft stool

claims.claim: Review barriers to school toilet access
claims.source_text: Review toilet access eg investigate barriers to using school toilets

claims.claim: Excessive cow milk may exacerbate constipation
claims.source_text: Excessive cow milk intake may result in inadequate dietary fibre; this may exacerbate constipation in some children

claims.claim: First line agents by age
claims.source_text: Infants … 1 month: Coloxyl drops … Infants 1-12 months: Iso-osmotic laxative (Macrogol-3350 + electrolytes or Lactulose … Children: Iso-osmotic laxative or lubricant (paraffin oil)

claims.claim: Withholding or fissures may need inpatient disimpaction
claims.source_text: Children with stool withholding behaviours, pain while defecating or rectal bleeding or fissures may benefit from inpatient disimpaction management

claims.claim: Petroleum jelly for anal fissure pain
claims.source_text: Anal fissures can be treated with topical Petroleum Jelly to provide pain relief

claims.claim: Lactulose maintenance dosing row
claims.source_text: Lactulose … Osmotic laxative … 1-12 mo 3-5 mL/day … 1-5 yo 5-10 mL/day … 5-14 yo 10-40 mL/day … Split larger doses bd

claims.claim: Coloxyl drops dosing row and senna caution
claims.source_text: 0.3 mL tds … 6-18 mo 0.5 mL tds … 18 mo-3 yo 0.8 mL tds … Coloxyl+Senna: Senna is the stimulant component and should be avoided unless stools are soft, >2 yo

claims.claim: Macrogol with electrolytes dosing row and PBS status
claims.source_text: 1-12 mo ½ sachet daily … 1-6 yo 1 sachet daily (max 2/day) … 6-12 yo 1-2 sachets daily (max 2/day) … 12 yo 1-4 sachets/day … PBS listed (authority not required)

claims.claim: Macrogol 3350 scoop dosing row
claims.source_text: 2-6 yo 1 small scoop/day … 6-12 yo 1 large scoop/day … 12 yo 1-2 large scoops/day … Tin with double ended scoop - large (17 g) and small (8.5 g)

claims.claim: Paraffin oil dosing row and cautions
claims.source_text: 1-6 yo 10-15 mL/day … 6-12 yo 15-20 mL/day … 12 yo up to 40 mL/day … Can cause orange oil seepage in underwear (reduce dosage) … Avoid in children with swallowing problems due to aspiration risk, particularly those <6 mo

claims.claim: Stimulant dosing row and cautions
claims.source_text: 6 mo-4 yo, 0.25 mg/kg (max 5 mg = 10 drops) nocte … 4-10 yo 5-10 drops nocte … 10 yo 10 drops nocte or 1-2 tablets nocte … Useful for patients who cannot tolerate large volumes of liquid. Avoid if impacted … Can cause abdominal cramps. Do not use long term

claims.claim: Disimpaction precedes maintenance and oral outpatient is preferred
claims.source_text: Children with severe constipation benefit from a disimpaction regimen before maintenance treatment begins … Oral medication as an outpatient is effective and preferred. Switch to maintenance therapy immediately post disimpaction

claims.claim: Suppository or enema only as a one-off with sedation considered
claims.source_text: Only consider the use of glycerine suppository or Microlax™ enema as a one off treatment. Sedation should be strongly considered

claims.claim: Review disimpaction need on day 4
claims.source_text: It is recommended to review ongoing need for disimpaction on day 4 of treatment

claims.claim: Macrogol sachet disimpaction schedule
claims.source_text: Number of Macrogol-3350 + electrolytes sachets (adult formulation) Age Day 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 1-6 yo 1 2 2 3 3 4 4 6-12 yo 2 3 4 5 6 6 6 12+ yo 8 8 8

claims.claim: Movicol Junior equivalence
claims.source_text: 1 sachet Macrogol-3350 with electrolytes adult formulation = 2 sachets of "Movicol Junior" formulation

claims.claim: OsmoLax scoop disimpaction schedule
claims.source_text: Number of OsmoLax ™ small scoops (8.5 g) Age Day 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 2-6 yo 2 3 3 4 5 6 6 6-12 yo 3 4 6 8 9 9 9

claims.claim: Inpatient NGT washout rate
claims.source_text: Macrogol/ electrolyte solutions (Colonlytely™, Glycoprep™) 1-3 L/day, via NGT at a rate of 25 mL/kg/hr (maximum rate 400 mL/hr, or less depending on pump used)

claims.claim: Washout solutions provide no net fluid input
claims.source_text: Normal maintenance oral fluids should be given in addition to maintain hydration. These solutions provide no net fluid input and there is a risk of dehydration

claims.claim: Sodium picosulphate fixed dose regimens
claims.source_text: Children 4-9 yo: 1 sachet - first dose / ½ sachet - second dose (=15 mg sodium picosulphate/day) … Children >9 yo: 1 sachet BD (= 20 mg sodium picosulphate/day)

claims.claim: Do not use in obstruction or renal impairment; cease on clear fluid PR
claims.source_text: Do not use if signs of obstruction or in renal impairment … Consider ceasing if child begins passing clear fluid per rectum

claims.claim: Oral medication may be flushed without absorption during washout
claims.source_text: Oral medication taken during or within the hour before administration of a bowel washout may be flushed from the gastrointestinal tract without absorption

claims.claim: Follow up within 4 weeks and continence service referral
claims.source_text: Arrange follow up with GP or paediatrician within 4 weeks. … Consider referral to a continence or encopresis service for faecal/urinary incontinence, complex or difficult cases

claims.claim: Paediatric consultation triggers
claims.source_text: Red flags present, or concerns of an underlying organic pathology … Non-resolution occurs despite optimising management over 6 months (outpatient) … Outpatient disimpaction fails, requiring inpatient management

claims.claim: Last updated March 2020
claims.source_text: Last updated March 2020
